info.text:
October consumer prices rose 0.4% in a month, hotter than expected, and wholesale prices are up 6.5% over a year, and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point December hike should be considered if core inflation stayed hot. Yet Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate fell for a fourth straight week, to 7.11%, while the dollar hit a 19-month high and the yen slid back near 160. This video explains why mortgage rates move before the Fed does, who wins and loses from a strong dollar, and what a December hike would mean for your credit card, mortgage, savings and paycheck.
